title: Improvement Plan for Series-Parallel Graph Scheduler
description: Raise the scheduler from a solid local tool to a more robust, maintainable, and safer codebase by tightening graph validation, CLI input handling, lock behavior, visualizer safety, tooling, and verification.

scheduler.claimPolicy: A session may claim only ready leaf nodes. Parent nodes describe series or parallel composition; child leaves are the units of work.
scheduler.slackPolicy: Use chat for attention and approvals when configured. Canonical state remains in this graph file.

ROOT.title: Improve scheduler robustness and maintainability
ROOT.description: Establish the current baseline, then run independent hardening branches in parallel before integrating the changes and performing final verification.

BASELINE.title: Confirm baseline behavior and improvement scope
BASELINE.description: Capture the current working state and turn the review findings into concrete implementation boundaries before touching runtime behavior.

IMP1.title: Record baseline commands and risks
IMP1.description: Run the current authoritative checks and write a short baseline report covering the commands, observed results, dirty working tree considerations, and the main risks being addressed.
deliverables: A report listing exact baseline commands and results for npm test, npm run typecheck, npm run build, and smoke:migration if practical.
A short risk list covering unchecked graph JSON, permissive CLI number parsing, filesystem lock races, visualizer worker APIs, and missing lint/CI automation.
acceptanceCriteria: Baseline command results are recorded with pass/fail status.
Any pre-existing failure or dirty working tree concern is explicitly called out.
No runtime code is changed as part of this task.

IMP2.title: Define compatibility boundaries
IMP2.description: Document the public behavior that must remain compatible while the hardening branches proceed.
deliverables: A compatibility note covering CLI command names, JSON output shapes, graph state semantics, visualizer endpoints, worker execution, generated reports, and renderer output locations.
A short list of allowed behavior changes, such as clearer validation errors for invalid input.
acceptanceCriteria: Workers can use the note to avoid accidental CLI or graph schema breakage.
The note identifies which changes require updating README examples or tests.
The plan remains compatible with the existing scheduler graph format.

HARDENING.title: Parallel hardening work
HARDENING.description: Independent branches that can be worked on at the same time after the baseline is known.

GRAPH_VALIDATION.title: Graph file validation branch
GRAPH_VALIDATION.description: Use the existing runtime validators consistently so malformed graph files fail early with useful errors.

IMP3.title: Route graph reads through runtime validation
IMP3.description: Update graph loading paths to parse JSON as unknown, call the existing graph validator, and return typed graph data only after validation succeeds.
deliverables: readGraph validates parsed graph files before returning them.
Renderer graph loading applies equivalent validation or shares the same helper.
Validation errors include the graph path and validator issue details.
acceptanceCriteria: Valid existing graph files still load and render.
Malformed graph files fail before traversal or mutation logic runs.
No broad schema expansion is introduced beyond the existing graph contract unless tests require it.

IMP4.title: Expand graph validation coverage
IMP4.description: Add focused tests for invalid graph shapes and unknown child references in CLI, renderer, and direct readGraph usage.
deliverables: Tests for missing graph body, missing root, missing nodes map, unknown child ids, and invalid children arrays.
Assertions that validation errors are readable and stable enough for operators.
acceptanceCriteria: npm test covers invalid graph loading paths.
Tests prove valid fixture graphs continue to work.
Error messages do not expose stack traces in normal CLI output beyond the current CLI behavior expectations.

IMP5.title: Document graph validation expectations
IMP5.description: Update README guidance so operators and workers know what the scheduler validates and what graph authoring mistakes are rejected.
deliverables: README section or command note describing graph validation behavior.
Example invalid graph cases summarized in plain language.
acceptanceCriteria: Documentation matches the implemented validation behavior.
Existing quickstart examples remain correct.
No generated dist files are documented as source files.

CLI_VALIDATION.title: CLI input validation branch
CLI_VALIDATION.description: Make command-line parsing fail clearly for invalid numeric and structured inputs.

IMP6.title: Validate numeric CLI arguments
IMP6.description: Replace permissive Number(...) parsing with explicit validation for lease seconds, idle milliseconds, ports, worker counts, and similar numeric fields.
deliverables: A shared numeric argument helper that rejects missing, NaN, infinite, negative, and out-of-range values as appropriate.
Clear error messages naming the invalid flag and expected range.
acceptanceCriteria: Valid current CLI examples still work.
Invalid values such as --lease nope and --port NaN fail deterministically.
Tests cover the new validation behavior.

IMP7.title: Tighten structured CLI input errors
IMP7.description: Improve validation around repeated flags, child JSON, empty child ids, and boolean flags that accidentally receive values.
deliverables: More precise tests for --child, --child-json, --codex-arg, and command-specific required fields.
Small parser refinements only where they reduce ambiguous behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Existing supported invocation styles remain supported.
Invalid child definitions produce actionable errors.
No new dependency is introduced solely for argument parsing unless the existing parser becomes meaningfully simpler.

LOCKING.title: Filesystem lock hardening branch
LOCKING.description: Reduce race risk around stale lock cleanup and make lock failures easier to diagnose.

IMP8.title: Make lock ownership observable
IMP8.description: Add minimal metadata to graph lock directories so stale lock cleanup and timeout messages can report which process created the lock and when.
deliverables: A lock metadata file containing pid, createdAt, graphPath, and optional host information when available.
Timeout and stale-lock errors that include useful metadata when present.
acceptanceCriteria: Lock acquisition still works on plain local filesystems.
Existing stale lock tests pass or are updated to assert the richer metadata behavior.
No lock metadata is left behind after successful lock release.

IMP9.title: Test concurrent mutation behavior
IMP9.description: Add stress-oriented tests around simultaneous claims, stale lock cleanup, and lock timeout behavior.
deliverables: A test that concurrent claim attempts do not claim the same ready leaf.
A test that timeout behavior remains bounded and readable.
A test that stale lock cleanup does not leave temporary files behind.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests are deterministic enough for local and CI execution.
The suite stays fast and avoids long sleeps.
Failure output points to the graph path or lock path involved.

VISUALIZER_SAFETY.title: Visualizer safety branch
VISUALIZER_SAFETY.description: Keep the visualizer useful as a local operator tool while reducing accidental exposure and unsafe worker starts.

IMP10.title: Clarify local-only server posture
IMP10.description: Make the visualizer's localhost-oriented security model explicit in code and documentation.
deliverables: README wording that the worker manager API is intended for trusted local use.
A startup warning or help text when binding to a non-local host.
acceptanceCriteria: Default host remains 127.0.0.1.
Binding to 0.0.0.0 or a non-local address makes the risk visible to the operator.
Existing visualizer tests still pass.

IMP11.title: Constrain visualizer worker inputs
IMP11.description: Add server-side validation for worker manager requests so count, paths, commands, and argument arrays are bounded and predictable.
deliverables: Validation for count, idleMs, leaseSeconds, cwd, codexCommand, codexArgs length, and string sizes.
Readable HTTP 400 responses for invalid worker start requests.
acceptanceCriteria: Current worker manager happy-path tests still pass.
Invalid request tests cover oversized or malformed fields.
The API does not spawn a process when validation fails.

IMP12.title: Review browser-rendered HTML safety
IMP12.description: Audit visualizer and static renderer HTML insertion paths, especially graph SVG, worker logs, and graph-provided text.
deliverables: A short audit note listing each innerHTML use and why it is safe or how it was fixed.
Tests proving graph labels, worker logs, and document fields are escaped where needed.
acceptanceCriteria: No untrusted graph text can inject script through normal visualizer or renderer output.
Legitimate SVG graph rendering still works.
Existing escaping tests remain green.

TOOLING.title: Tooling and automation branch
TOOLING.description: Add lightweight project hygiene without turning this focused tool into a framework-heavy package.

IMP13.title: Add lint or formatting guard
IMP13.description: Introduce a minimal linting or formatting check that fits the existing TypeScript and Node setup.
deliverables: A package script such as npm run lint or npm run format:check.
Configuration kept small and compatible with the current code style.
acceptanceCriteria: The new script runs locally without changing unrelated generated files.
npm test remains focused on typecheck, build, and behavior tests unless the project intentionally folds lint into test.
README command list is updated if a new authoritative check is added.

IMP14.title: Add CI workflow for authoritative checks
IMP14.description: Add a simple CI workflow that installs dependencies and runs the project checks on pull requests or pushes.
deliverables: A GitHub Actions workflow or documented equivalent for npm ci and npm test.
Optional lint/typecheck step if separate from npm test.
acceptanceCriteria: The workflow uses Node 20 or newer.
The workflow avoids secrets and does not require Slack or Codex credentials.
Local npm test behavior remains unchanged.

INTEGRATION_GATE.title: Integrate hardening branches
INTEGRATION_GATE.description: Confirm the parallel branches work together and resolve any collisions in tests, docs, CLI behavior, or shared helper modules.
deliverables: All branch changes integrated without duplicated helper logic.
README and package scripts reflect the final authoritative workflow.
A short integration report summarizing compatibility impact.
acceptanceCriteria: npm run typecheck passes.
npm run build passes.
npm test passes.
No generated dist or HTML churn is included unless intentionally regenerated.

FINAL_VERIFY.title: Final verification and release notes
FINAL_VERIFY.description: Run the full verification path and leave future operators with a clear summary of what changed.

IMP15.title: Run full verification suite
IMP15.description: Run all authoritative checks after integration and capture the results.
deliverables: Final command output summary for npm run typecheck, npm run build, npm test, and smoke:migration if available.
A note explaining any skipped check.
acceptanceCriteria: All required checks pass or any failure is explicitly blocked for operator decision.
The final graph and docs remain valid JSON/Markdown.
No unexpected graph state files, lock directories, or temporary files are left behind.

IMP16.title: Write improvement summary
IMP16.description: Produce a concise final summary suitable for a commit message, pull request body, or operator handoff.
deliverables: Summary of implemented improvements grouped by validation, CLI UX, locking, visualizer safety, tooling, and tests.
Residual risks and suggested next improvements, if any.
acceptanceCriteria: The summary references the final verification results.
Residual risks are honest and specific.
The project is left in a state where a reviewer can evaluate the changes quickly.
